$comment: Full evaluation campaign — every pillar from the dissertation evaluation plan.
Designed for HPC: each task runs independently under SLURM array; aggregator combines.
Most baseline / variant / ablation experiments use simbench_lv_constrained_45 so the slack
budget is tight enough that variant outcomes are actually distinguishable.  Cascading,
scaling, cold-day stress and generator-failure experiments live in their own sections.
Reconfiguration uses simbench_lv_reconfig (same grid + 5 backup branches per sector).
Pillar 9 (cp_flexibility) uses the cp_size_multiplier / replace_primary_generation knobs
of monee's MES generator to construct grids where coupling-point capacity is load-bearing
for resilience: simbench_lv_cp_heavy_45 inflates CP rated output 2x (additive); cp_dependent_45
keeps CP at 1x but absorbs primary-gen output to keep total per-carrier production invariant
(losing a CP now disables both the unit and the displaced primary gen); cp_heavy_dependent_45
combines both knobs.  Also exercises the new failure_type=concentrated picker which clusters
branch failures around a load-rich node to produce per-group capacity asymmetry.
name: eval_full

experiments.$comment: Pillar 1 — Functional restoration quality.  Three slack budgets show the curve from loose (60 %) to tight (30 %).  Skewed priority distribution exercises the priority-weighted served metric properly.
experiments.name: functional_baseline

experiments.$comment: Pillar 2 — Optimality gap.  Pairs every scare run with an oracle on the same (grid, seed).
experiments.name: optimality_gap

experiments.$comment: Pillar 3 — variant comparison: scare vs single-level (gossip only) vs oracle.
experiments.name: variant_comparison

experiments.$comment: Pillar 4 — ablation matrix.  One ablation per architectural component.  Run on concentrated failures so the architecture has work to do.
experiments.name: ablation

experiments.$comment: Cold-day thermal stress — narrows heat sector against its lower bound; CP plants matter when they can convert gas/power to extra heat output.
experiments.name: cold_day_stress

experiments.$comment: Generator-class failures — the historical CP-flexibility scenario.  Compares branch / generator / mixed contingency populations.
experiments.name: generator_failure

$comment: Pillar 7 — Scaling.  Three simbench LV variants spanning roughly a decade of node count:
small  ≈   36 nodes (1-LV-rural1)
medium ≈  137 nodes (1-LV-semiurb4)
large  ≈  396 nodes (1-LV-rural3, the established benchmark)
All run with the same 45 % slack budget so the only varying axis is grid size.
experiments.name: scaling

$comment: Pillar 8 — Reconfiguration.  Uses simbench_lv_reconfig: the constrained LV grid
augmented with 5 normally-open backup branches per sector (15 total).  Failures
bias toward branches because the reconfiguration pathway only fires on
BranchFailureEvent; generator failures don't test reconfiguration.
experiments.name: reconfiguration

$comment: Pillar 9 — CP flexibility shift.  The headline experiment for the cross-sector ADMM
layer.  Uses three new grid variants built with monee's cp_size_multiplier and
replace_primary_generation knobs:
cp_heavy_45            : CP rated output 2x, additive (loss of CP recoverable)
cp_dependent_45        : CP rated output 1x, replaces primary gen (loss of CP
disables BOTH the unit and the displaced primary gen)
cp_heavy_dependent_45  : both knobs combined (maximum cross-carrier dependence)
On the dependent variants, gossip + islanding alone cannot recover from a CP
failure because the displaced primary gen is gone — the cross-sector ADMM is
the only path to compensate.
Failures: generator-class so CPs themselves are part of the failure population.
experiments.name: cp_flexibility

$comment: Concentrated imbalance.  failure_type=concentrated picks a load-rich node and
BFS-walks outward, producing spatially-clustered failures that target one
sub-community with stark deficit while neighbours retain slack capacity.
This is the test designed to surface the holonic ADMM's inter-group
redistribution; on the cp_heavy_dependent grid the CP-ADMM may also engage.
experiments.name: concentrated_imbalance

experiments.$comment: CP-size sweep — measures how PWSF varies with CP rated output on the dependent variant.  Replaces the old todo for sizing studies.
experiments.name: cp_size_sweep
